verdict.tagline: Polished brawler trapped behind heavy technical flaws and aggressive monetization.
for_you_if: you want cinematic story chapters and flashy combat
you have the patience to master complex fighting mechanics
not_for_you_if: you are unwilling to wait through lengthy shader compilation
you cannot accept microtransactions and expensive character packs
you require stable performance without constant stutters

Honestly, I really wanted to like MK1, but it just didn't click with me.

The story feels unnecessarily messed up and chaotic, and the overall vibe isn't really my taste. MK11 had that dark, brutal atmosphere that made the game feel like Mortal Kombat. MK1 feels much more vibrant and colorful, which takes away some of that appeal for me.

I also prefer MK11's story, presentation, and overall experience by a lot.

The PC optimization is another major issue. The game can look great, but the performance and optimization just aren't where they should be.

And after finishing the story, there's not much that keeps me interested. It quickly becomes repetitive and boring, especially if you're mainly playing offline.

MK1 isn't a terrible fighting game, but compared to MK11, it feels like a downgrade to me. I'd recommend waiting for a heavy discount if you're still interested.

claims.claim: The story mode receives mixed reactions, with reviewers praising the initial chapters and presentation but criticizing the second half for feeling rushed and introducing a multiverse plotline.

citations.review_text:
Kampaign Rating- 7.2/10 (*Including the Story DLC Expansion) 

The Kampaign starts off really well with gorgeous visuals, a fresh take on familar characters, and an interesting reboot. Sadly, the second half feels rushed, and bringing back the multiverse/ timeline story takes away from what could have been a great reboot. It had much more potential.

I play Mortal Kombat since MK9 and I really liked its comeback to 2D roots. MK1 is not a terrible game, but I feel obliged to leave negative review for the sake of the future of the series. 

What I like about MK1:
- keeping relatively realistic design from MK11 (and its slower pace, which suits me more)
- brining back some quite forgotten characters from 3D era, my favorite being Ashrah (not as good as Fujin in MK11, though)

What I didn't like:
- The plot was quite compelling until the "grand reveal" - from that point it went downhill very fast and the last chapter is completely ridicoulus. In general, I feel that using multiple timelines as a plot device makes events and decision less significant and it was already evident in MK11. MK1 takes this to another level, populating alternate timelines with palette swaps and weird hybrids of known characters.
- Speaking of the plot, the chapter structure of main campaign also feels worn out. We obviously play as "good guys" versus "bad gays", which means that we fight the same small group of jobbers again and again. For once, at least, Reptile and Baraka aren't punching bags, which might be the greatest plot twist.
- Invasions mode is... not great. It quickly becomes repetitive and adds nothing to the overall experience. Some challenges are fun, but in total it's quite boring and feels like grinding. 
- Lack of brand-new kombatants may be a safe choice, but it may be also sign of a creative dead end.

In 2026 the "Definitive Edition" is a good deal, ESPECIALLY if you get it on sale. I can see why people had problems with the monetization and such when the game first game out, because it doesn't seem like there was much there for the price of the game. But I bought this for $20, a couple years after the game initial release.

Don't let the complaints get to you. If you're not the sort of person that's worried about being hyper-competitive online, and just like some hack and slash fighting fun, then this is a good game. A REALLY good game. After what I'm sure was many patches, the game looks good, runs well, it's fun, and it has dozens of hours of unlockable content to grind at if that's what you like in these games (and for me, it is). The highlight though has to be the story. Again, don't let the complainers get to you - the quality of the story mode, especially Part 1, is pretty top notch. It feels like the that quippy, Marvel-movie style writing, but it fits the genre here and makes it way more entertaining than it has any right to be.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the PC version suffers from technical issues, including constant stutters and lengthy shader compilation times when settings are changed.

citations.review_text: worst MK game to exist. every time I load into a game, it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stutters for no reason. I play at 1080p on the lowest settings with dlss set to quality, and even then it stutters a lot. if I change any settings and load back into the game, it makes me sit through shader compilation. the pc optimization is terrible constant stuttering completely ruins the gameplay, and having to wait for shaders to compile every time i change a setting is just frustrating. its supposed to feel smooth and responsive but it feels like i am fighting my PC instead. i will never recommend this game to anyone to play on the pc.

NetherRealm Studios made a fighting game and then remembered they also need to monetize every breath players take. MK1 is what happens when you've got a solid foundation and then bury it under cosmetic DLC, battle pass grinds, paid fatalities (yes, really), and a PC port that's actively hostile to anyone trying to run it.

The core fighting is actually fine — it's familiar dial-a-combo MK on a prettier engine. But everything surrounding it exists to either milk you or frustrate you into submission. The story mode is competent at best, the character roster feels lean compared to MK11, and the whole thing was supposedly a "soft reboot" that managed to be less ambitious than a game that came out in 2019. The gore is weirdly toned down (seriously, who asked for that in a Mortal Kombat game?), the Kameo assist system is janky, and there's no cross-play because Warner Bros. wants to keep you on a specific platform.

On PC, the performance is a dumpster fire. High-end rigs stutter, menu loads are glacial, and you get a benchmarking screen before every online match for reasons nobody can explain. It's a decade-old engine running like it learned to code from a self-help book.

By April 2024, the Steam player count had collapsed to subsistence levels. The competitive community migrated back to MK11 or over to Street Fighter 6. It's not that MK1 is broken — it's that it's cynically designed and half-finished while demanding your $60 and constant nibbles at your wallet.

Play Street Fighter 6 instead. It costs the same, respects your time, and doesn't act like it's punishing you for owning a PC.

citations.review_text: Good game but im mad about the shaders pre loading. I work a 9 to 7 job so i dont get much time to play and i dont even play much cuz of work, somtimes I get free time in between my work so launch the game and get shaders pre loading taking away the free time. At first it was ok, I can wait for a bit then proceed to play it, but the game goes to load the shaders again and again every 2-3 days, even playing the game while the shaders are loading in backgound is hassle cuz it lags too much.

There's a lot to be said here.

First, let me just note something for you to keep in mind during this read. That is: I bought this game at full price on launch day but hadn't picked it up until after 3 years. Because of this, I missed the disaster that was the launch, the bugs (especially the player 1 advantage bug) the balancing issues, etc. Many players speculate that this was a rushed game due to the fact that during development, this was originally an Injustice game, until they decided to switch gears.

After 3 years has this improved? Tremendously. 100% No. For example, I can run the in-game benchmark and hit a solid 60 FPS with no sweat every single time (at max settings, with Nvidia DLAA enabled).  However while watching my FPS counter during single player, I've seen my FPS dip to as low as 54 for a split second. Considering the hardware I have, this shouldn't occur, and that goes a long with every other modern title. Is that enough to break the pace of the game and cause a brief stutter or freeze? No. It also happens very minimally, though it shouldn't happen at all. Other than than that, the game maintains a solid 60 FPS. A positive I'll say here about performance is that while playing online, wifi players are nowhere near the pain in the ass they were in MK11 and MKX. The freezing in those scenarios, while it didn't happen ALL the time, seems to have vastly diminished in MK1. At least this has been my case with many hours clocked online. Whatever they improved with the already good netcode, really has worked wonders here. I'll also note that two players can connect, both with poor pings (in the red) but because both players are wired, it poses no problem in the match. This seemed to be the case for MK11 as well. Bravo.

Moving on, I will acknowledge the main complaint about this game. The story. Complete trash. Yes, it's visually stunning, and well put together, but the end result is simply sub par. I found a lot of this had to do with the character retcon…
